the immunotherapeutic approach, based on TLR5 activation and IFNs, is able to reduce the metastatic growth in a murine model.
a new immunotherapic approach, based on TLR5 activation and IFNs production, is capable to control the lung metastatic growth of melanoma.
the combination of flagellin (TLR‐5 ligand) and immunomodulator P10, administered via the mucosal route, is capable of inducing an immune response that controls metastatic melanoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the mechanisms involved in the anti‐metastatic effect of flagellin in combination with P10, a major histocompatibility class II‐restricted antigen derived from the Parococcidioides Brasiliensis gp43, which is capable of inducing a proinflammatory response in the lungs of C57Bl/ 6 mice.
a new immunotherapy approach for melanoma treatment based on TLR5 ligand flagella combined with the P10 peptide.
the use of a new immunotherapy approach based on Tlr‐5 activation and Ifn‐γ production capable of controlling the metastatic growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intranasal administration of flagellain and P10 is a promising approach to reduce the number of metastases in a melanoma model, which may be used in association with chemotherapeutic agents for a more effective anti‐tumoral response.

our results report a novel immunotherapeutic strategy based on TLR5 stimulation and IFN‐g production able to control the metastasis of B16F1O‐Nex2 murine melanoma, being promising to be associated with chemotherapy drugs for a more effective anti‐tumoral response.

the combination of flagellin (TLR5 ligand) and P10 (a peptide derived from the major surface glycoprotein of Paracoccidiodes brasiliensis) administered intranasally to B16F10 melanoma‐bearing C57BL/6 mice resulted in an anti‐metastatic effect, as well as a significant increase in the mice survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of the TLR5 agonist flagellin (FliCi) with the immunomodulatory peptide P10 (derived from the Paracocidioides brasillensis major surface antigen gp43) induces an effective anti‐metastatic immune response against melanoma, which is dependent on the TLR5 signaling pathway.
we developed a new immunotherapetic approach based on TRL‐5 activation and interferon gamma production that is capable to control the growth of metastatic melanoma.
intranasal administration of FliC + P10 formulation in a melanoma metastatic model induced a systemic proinflammatory response that resulted in an anti‐metastatic effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

intranasal immunotherapy using flagellin (FliCi), a ligand for the Toll‐like‐receptor 5 (TLR‐5) combined with the immunomodulatory peptide P10, derived from the gp43 protein of Paracoccidiodes brasiliensis, reduced the number and volume of lung metastasis and increased survival of mice challenged intravenously with syngene B16F10 melanoma.

the intranasal administration of a formulation containing flagellin and P10 peptide can reduce the number of lung tumors in a melanoma model, and that this effect is dependent upon TLR‐5 and IFN‐gamma expression, but independent on caspase‐one activation.

intranasal administration of the TLR‐5 ligand Salmonella Typhimirum flagellin combined with the immunomodulatory peptide P10 is able to reduce the number of lung melanoma metastasis in a mouse model, and that this effect is mediated by TLR‐5 and IFN‐g signaling.
